summary: Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Yamagata High School, Taisho University, and Waseda University. He was a lecturer, assistant professor, and professor at Waseda University (1968–1998), and later served at Bunkyo Gakuin University.

Hideomi Yaita (b. 1953) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he later served as a lecturer (attested 1995), and worked as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies around 1986.
Hidetaka Fukazawa (b. 1956) is a religious studies scholar. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1975 to 1979 and held a post at Hitotsubashi University around 1993.
Hidetaka Nakatani specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under the supervision of Gadjin Nagao.
Hideto Ono (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

Hidetoshi Yoshizawa specializes in Buddhist studies. At Taisho University, he held posts as a researcher (attested 1998), research student (attested 2006), lecturer (attested 2008), and chief research fellow (attested 2017).

Hidetsugu Yagi (1886–1976) studied at Osaka Prefectural Kitano High School and the University of Tokyo (around 1907–1909). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University, Osaka University, and Tokyo Institute of Technology, and taught Arthur Waley.

Hideyo Ogawa (b. 1954) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He served as an assistant professor (around 1990–1998) and professor (around 1998–2020; attested 2026) at Hiroshima University, where he taught Shindo Kusumoto.

Hideyuki Matsumori works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Soka University (attested 2006), where he later held posts as an assistant professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).

Himanshu Prabha Ray (b. 1947) works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where she served as associate professor (c. 1980–2012). She also held posts at Munich and the National Monuments Authority.

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the University of Göttingen before holding a post at the University of Breslau from around 1813 to 1861, teaching Albrecht Weber.

Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia (b. 1894) worked in Indology and religious studies. In 1947, he was attested as Professor of Ardhamagadhi at MTB Arts College and as a Ph.D. teacher in Ardhamagadhi at the University of Mumbai.

Hiram W. Woodward (b. 1940) specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and Yale, he held academic posts at Silpakorn, Michigan, and Vermont, and served as curator of Asian art at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at DAV College and Oriental College, he served with the Archaeological Survey of India, as Government Epigraphist, and as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State (1934–1942).

Hirofumi Isoda (b. 1938) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Tohoku University by 1966, later serving there as a lecturer and associate professor, and was an honorary professor at Shimane University (attested 1974).

Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University from around 1978 to 2002 and was affiliated with the Lotus Sutra Institute.

Hiroko Kawanami works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott, and served as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016), where she taught Kan Boonyakanchana and Jianchengshi.

Hiroko Matsuoka works in Indology and philosophy. She pursued doctoral studies at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and held posts at the University of Leipzig (attested 2016) and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Hiromasa Tosaki (1930–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Kyushu University and studied at Harvard. He held posts at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College and Kyushu University, where he was a professor (c. 1978–1994).

Hiromi Habata (b. 1961) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg, she held posts at the University of Munich, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
